name: clipr
resume: All seven exports are done. Clipboard access calls xclip, then xsel, then wl-copy. Tables follow write.table and read.table. write_last_clip takes the value as an argument because Python has no .Last.value. clipr has no compiled code, so there is no crate.

functions.name: clear_clip
functions.done: Writes an empty string through write_clip.

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(clipr))
system2("xclip", c("-selection", "clipboard"), input = "seed")
write_clip("to-clear")

one <- function() clear_clip()
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
emptied <- read_clip()
cat(sprintf(
  "{\"value\":\"\",\"empty\":%s,\"median_ms\":%.17g}\n",
  if (is.null(emptied)) "true" else "false",
  median(elapsed) * 1000
))
proof.python:
import json
import statistics
import time
import warnings

from clipr import clear_clip, read_clip, write_clip

write_clip("to-clear")


def one():
    return clear_clip()


value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)

with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
    emptied = read_clip()

print(json.dumps({
    "value": value,
    "empty": emptied is None,
    "median_ms": statistics.median(elapsed),
}))

functions.name: read_clip
functions.done: Reads the clipboard and splits on newlines, including blank lines. Empty text returns None.

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(clipr))
system2("xclip", c("-selection", "clipboard"), input = "seed")
write_clip(c("Write", "to", "clipboard"))

json_escape <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\", "\\\\", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("\"", "\\\"", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("\n", "\\n", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("\t", "\\t", x, fixed = TRUE)
  paste0("\"", x, "\"")
}

one <- function() read_clip()
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(sprintf(
  "{\"value\":[%s],\"median_ms\":%.17g}\n",
  paste(vapply(value, json_escape, ""), collapse = ","),
  median(elapsed) * 1000
))

functions.name: write_clip
functions.done: Renders text and tables the way write.table does, then writes them with xclip, xsel, or wl-copy.

check.case: data.frame(a = c(1, 2, 3), b = c(4, 5, 6)), return_new = TRUE

proof.r:
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(clipr))
system2("xclip", c("-selection", "clipboard"), input = "seed")

json_escape <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\", "\\\\", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("\"", "\\\"", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("\r", "\\r", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("\n", "\\n", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("\t", "\\t", x, fixed = TRUE)
  paste0("\"", x, "\"")
}

one <- function() {
  write_clip(data.frame(a = c(1, 2, 3), b = c(4, 5, 6)), return_new = TRUE)
}
value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
cat(sprintf(
  "{\"value\":%s,\"median_ms\":%.17g}\n",
  json_escape(value),
  median(elapsed) * 1000
))

functions.name: write_last_clip
functions.done: Writes the caller-supplied value. Python has no .Last.value.

check.case: .Last.value is "Write to clipboard"; Python passes that string
